messages.subject: Multimarker model using MS stat
parts:
I am working on a project that aims to detect multimarker model for breast cancer progression prediction. 
I have the Ms data and trying to build the multimarker model and I wonder if MS stat have the code that can build this model from our data. 
Our data composed of markers intensities in both cases and control and we are planning to build a model which is made of the best combined markers that have the highest  sensitivity and specificity rate.
We've already built the pairwise model using logisitc regression where we judge the robustness of the paired marker based on the ROC curve they produce compared to their single ROC. 
Now we are planning to try every single possible combination and evaluate the effect of adding a marker on the ROC. 

For example: 
If a marker A has an AUC(Area under the curve of 0.7), then adding marker B improved the AUC to 0.78. Adding marker C to the already combined (A+B) reduces the AUC to 0.7, than we should not consider marker C in this combination and we can move to evaluate adding marker D to ( A+B) and so on . We consider the markers that when combined, the AUC of the combined markers is improving. 

Any suggestions?

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Multimarker model using MS stat
parts:
Dear Adhari,

MSstats is only designed for class comparison (i.e., testing), and not for class prediction (i.e., supervised classification such as logistic regression). However, you can use the 'subject quantification' part of the workflow, to obtain one number per protein per subject. These can be used as inputs to logistic regression, or to any other classification model.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Sincerely
Olga
